problems: Red/green shirt shapes, straight blue/tan trousers and regular boot bands dominate the everyday kits. Small hide patches do not overcome the modern-clothing read.
Flintworker and Scout have almost identical torso silhouettes; their handheld tools do most of the differentiation. Hearthkeeper is also too close to this same template.
Gatherer's grass construction is not apparent in this view. The smooth cylindrical container reads as a manufactured pail rather than a woven gathering basket.
The caravan leader's square blue case resembles modern luggage. The hood and three small shells suggest a generic traveller, not an unmistakable visiting mammoth herder.
The Chief's antlers and skull staff successfully signal authority, but the mantle reads as rectangular boards rather than a substantial animal pelt.

Basket and luggage grips are not visibly continuous with their containers. Several tools sit alongside the arms without a convincing hand grip; broad shoulder pieces also need clearance checks during animation.
Tiny ties, pins, facial paint and bag markings cannot carry identity at stream scale. The supplied near-frontal view does not establish readability from the game's elevated camera.

GLOBAL, anachronism: no kit hides 'trousers' or 'shoes', so every figure (all 8 everyday renders, the Chief and the leader) stands on full-length blue or khaki trouser legs with black shoes. The 'boots' are boxes in the pants colour with pants:light cuff bands and thin accent:dark stripes, so they read as jeans with white socks and striped sneakers. The bible asks for bare skin and uneven fur boots. This is the biggest problem: the lower half of every figure is modern.

GLOBAL, 'today's clothes recoloured': the torsos are plain box tunics in the wearer's saturated shirt colour (red, green) over dark trousers. Nothing in the silhouette says hide, fur or grass: no ragged hems, no one-shoulder wrap, no fur collars, no lacing. The red-tunic-and-jeans and green-tunic-and-khakis figures read as a T-shirt and trousers.

GLOBAL, clipboard slab: almost every kit (Flintworker, Hearthkeeper, Scout, Chief, leader) has the same pale tilted shirt:light rectangle on the chest. At stream scale it reads as a clipboard or sheet of paper. It is also the strongest shape on each figure, so it makes them all look alike.

GLOBAL, top hats: the Hearthkeeper, Scout and Flintworker kits keep the wearer's own hair (or add a squared-off hair block), and the Hearthkeeper and Scout put a thin accent band at y 0.28. The result is a tall dark block with a coloured band at its base, which reads plainly as a stovepipe or top hat with a hatband (figures 5 to 8).

DISTINCTNESS: the Flintworker, Hearthkeeper and Scout share one silhouette: a box tunic, the pale chest slab, a belt, trousers and a long stick in the right hand (adze handle, digging stick, spear). Only the Gatherer differs, and it differs in the wrong way (see below). At stream scale three of the four kits are the same person with a different stick.

Flintworker: the adze head (#81847a box on armR at y +0.075) floats at shoulder height beside the head, running parallel to the handle, so it reads as a mallet or hammer, not a hafted adze. A pants-coloured box on armR at y -0.33 wraps the hand like a blue mitten. A loose shirt-coloured box on the hips at [-0.105,-0.055,0.11] and a pants:light box at x -0.255 hang over the thigh as stray floating blocks and will clip when the leg swings.

Gatherer: the hide skirt is in the pants colour and the legs are not hidden, so the skirt runs straight into same-colour trouser legs. With the round accent 'buttons' on the belt line it reads as denim dungarees. The basket is a big smooth cylinder in accent (slate grey or navy) with a rim and a horizontal bar handle: a modern bucket, which is an explicit anachronism. The grass cape uses shirt-role colours, so it reads as cloth, not straw, and from the front it is invisible. The two shoulder boxes (0.37 deep, one shirt and one shirt:light) look like a book or shoulder pads.

Hearthkeeper: the shirt-coloured tunic, plain stick, accent headband over the wearer's own hair (a top hat) and a grey accent box on the right shoulder read as a modern labourer. The 'folded shoulder hide' cape is behind the figure and does not show from the front. The bone awl at the chest is a tiny pale cylinder that reads as a cigarette or piece of chalk.

Young Ridge Scout: the spear is the best prop in the set, but the figure is otherwise the Flintworker again (tunic, chest slab, belt, trousers). The feather (0.045 thick) is invisible. The pouch box at hips [0.18,-0.06,0.19] hangs in front of the thigh and will clip on every stride.

Chief: the antlers work, but the bone-topped staff's skull box and horn cones sit at the same height right beside the left antler, so the two merge into one clutter of pale sticks. The headdress base is a flat cream box in the 'hat' colour (a box hat), with a black hair strip under it. The ochre face marks are two small horizontal red patches on the cheeks, which read as rosy blush, not paint. The mantle front is again the brown-and-pale chest slabs, and the dark brown trouser legs make the lower half a suit. The shoulders are not much wider than an everyday figure's, so the mantle is not grand.

Leader: the 'beard' (hair:dark box 0.23x0.17 on the face at y -0.005) renders as a gaping black mouth, so the herder looks like they are screaming. The shell beads are three big cream spheres in a row that read as snowman buttons. The hide bundle is a blue pants-coloured box with a teal chevron on the front: a cool-box or lunchbox with a logo. The hood is a squared hat-coloured box with side slabs that reads as a blonde bob wig or helmet, not a hood. 'Patchwork' is one pale chest slab. Blue jeans legs again.
fix:
All kits: replace the exposed modern shirt/trouser treatment with visibly constructed hide, fur or plant-fibre garments. Hide default sleeves where they remain visible; use skin-matched bare limbs or individually fitted hide leggings, not recoloured jeans. Keep rigid lower panels clear of moving legs. Flintworker of the Sinew Seam: make the hide wrap distinctly one-shouldered with a stepped, uneven hem; enlarge the flint head and its binding into one readable tool silhouette, seat the shaft through the hand, and retain the asymmetric calf wraps. Overlapping-Grass Gatherer: bring the layered grass mantle over the shoulders so its stepped fringe is visible from above; replace the smooth pail with a squat basket using a few broad woven bands and a continuous handle attached at both sides. Hearthkeeper in the Folded Shoulder Hide: remove the visible default sleeves, enlarge the folded hide into a single thick asymmetric shoulder drape, and give the lower wrap a longer, clearly different outline; keep the pin seated against the fold and the staff gripped. Young Ridge Scout: shorten the hide wrap, expose more limb or use minimal fitted wraps, remove the apron-like front rectangle, and strengthen the stone spearhead and binding; keep this the lightest, narrowest silhouette. Chief of the Great Branched Antlers: preserve the antlers and skull staff, reshape the slab collar into overlapping pelt lobes with a chunky irregular edge, and anchor every antler branch visibly into the hide headpiece. Far-Roving Shell-Cowl Mammoth Herder: replace the case with a rounded hide pack on a connected strap, broaden the fur cowl, and add a large ivory tusk toggle or paired tusk ornaments visible from above; retain shells as secondary regional decoration. Re-render both body variants at the actual 40-degree town camera and thumbnail scale, including an arm-swing pose to check grips, shoulders and leg clearance. / ALL KITS: (a) Add "trousers" and "shoes" to every hide list. Give each leg fur boots on legL and legR in FIXED fur colours: a main boot box [0.23,0.30,0.26] at [0,-0.66,0.02] in #987052 (or #76513b), plus an uneven cuff box [0.25,0.07,0.28] at [0,-0.50,0.02] rotated z ±0.12 in #c3a575. Use different cuff tilts left and right so they look hand-made. Leave skin bare between the hem and the boot. (b) Remove the pale shirt:light chest slab from every kit. (c) Add "hair" to every hide list and author low, shaggy hair: a top slab about [0.33,0.08,0.30] at y 0.33, plus side and back locks that hang to the jaw. Put any headband at forehead level, [0.32,0.05,0.30] at y 0.24, never on the crown. (d) Make hems ragged: end each tunic or skirt with 2 or 3 overlapping boxes of different lengths, each rotated z ±0.08 to 0.15. (e) Use role colours for the main hide, and FIXED material colours (#e1d3ae, #c3a575, #987052, #76513b, #a8ad68) for fur trims, straw, bone, cord and boots, so the material reads as hide, fur or grass whatever the wearer's colours.

FLINTWORKER: make it a sleeveless ONE-SHOULDER hide wrap. Use a torso box [0.48,0.50,0.30] at y 0.25 that stops below the armpits, plus a wide strap box [0.14,0.62,0.32] rotated z 0.55 that runs from the right shoulder to the left hip (bare left shoulder). Add a short hide skirt [0.50,0.30,0.32] at y -0.08 with a ragged hem, and a braided belt. Keep the tied top-knot. Rebuild the adze: a handle cylinder about 0.5 long hanging from the hand (centre y -0.62), with the stone head as a box [0.22,0.08,0.09] at the BOTTOM end, set crosswise (perpendicular to the handle). Delete the blue hand box and the two stray hip blocks. Add a small flint-nodule pouch: a sphere in #81847a on the belt at x 0.18, z 0.17, inside 0.12 m of the body.

GATHERER: make the GRASS CAPE the silhouette from every angle. On the cape bone, use 5 or 6 straw strips in #a8ad68, #c3a575 and #7c9254, each 0.12 wide and 0.65 to 0.75 long, fanned with rotation z -0.15 to +0.15. On hips, add a straw collar of short strips at y 0.55 that drapes over both shoulders and shows from the front (a fringe [0.56,0.12,0.36] made of 4 tilted boxes). Hide trousers. Make a hide skirt in a role colour down to the knee ([0.48,0.42,0.30] at y -0.15) with a ragged hem. Remove the overall-button spheres. Replace the bucket with a woven basket in #c3a575: a cone or tapered cylinder that is WIDER AT THE TOP ([0.26,0.24,0.26]), with 2 thin #987052 band rings and a cord loop handle (not a horizontal bar). Alternatively, carry it on the back on the cape bone so the shape shows from above.

HEARTHKEEPER: give this kit the long-dress silhouette. Use a hide shift on hips [0.50,0.95,0.32] centred y 0.10, reaching mid-shin, with a ragged hem, plus a thick FUR SHAWL across both shoulders in #e1d3ae ([0.60,0.16,0.40] at y 0.56, slightly rotated) that is visible from front and above. Keep the sleeves. Hide hair, then add a long hair braid down the back. In the right hand, replace the plain stick with something domestic: a hide water bag (sphere [0.18,0.22,0.14] in #987052 with a cord) or a bundle of firewood (3 short #76513b cylinders crossed). Delete the grey shoulder box and the chalk-like awl, or turn the awl into a bone pin holding the shawl, 0.10 long and visible at the collar.

SCOUT: make this the lean, bare-chested figure. Hide sleeves, trousers and shoes. Wear only a loincloth (front and back flaps [0.22,0.30,0.04]) and a WOLF/FOX PELT over one shoulder: a #987052 box [0.20,0.55,0.32] rotated z 0.35, with a tail cone hanging down the back. Put a skin-coloured bare torso showing on the other side by not covering the whole torso. Add low wrapped foot bindings. Keep the spear, but make it taller (2.0) and set its flint head in #81847a. Make the feather a real silhouette: 0.06 wide, 0.30 tall, upright at the back of the head in #e1d3ae with an ochre tip. Move the pouch to the belt at the side (x 0.24, y 0.0, inside 0.12 m) so it never crosses the leg.

CHIEF: separate the staff from the headdress. Either put the staff in the LEFT hand, or keep it in the right hand but lean it outward (rotation z 0.2) so the skull top sits clear of the antler, about 0.35 m to the side. Replace the flat cream hat box with a fur band ([0.36,0.10,0.32] at y 0.30, in #76513b, with a #e1d3ae fur rim). Enlarge the antlers to about 1.5x, with 3 tines per side, angled up and out to roughly 0.55 m above the head, and keep them asymmetric. Put 3 or 4 feathers 0.06 wide upright behind one antler. Face marks: 2 VERTICAL ochre stripes (#f07835) per cheek, plus a yellow ochre (#e9b04c) band across the brow, instead of the round blush. Mantle: a huge layered fur collar in #e1d3ae spanning 0.70 across the shoulders and 0.45 deep, with a second hide layer below it ending in a ragged hem at the knees. Add a necklace of 5 small #e1d3ae cones (teeth) at the collar. Hide trousers and add fur leggings/boots in #76513b. Remove the pale chest lapels and the tiny toggle.

LEADER: delete the black face box. If a beard is wanted, use the 'hair' role (not :dark), [0.20,0.12,0.06] at y 0.02, z 0.16, with its top edge below the mouth line. Make the hood a hood: a back panel and side panels in a role colour, a cone point at the back of the head (rotation x -0.6), and a fur rim in #e1d3ae around the face opening. Replace the 3 big buttons with a necklace arc of 8 or 9 small #e1d3ae spheres (size 0.045) from shoulder to shoulder at y 0.50 to 0.55. Replace the blue cool-box with a hide roll: a horizontal cylinder [0.14,0.36,0.14] (rotated z 1.57) in #987052, tied with 2 #76513b cords, with the foreign emblem as 2 small ochre (#f07835) rotated slats on its end. Add a large rolled hide bundle on the back (cape bone, #c3a575) so the traveller reads from above. Make the patchwork 4 or 5 patch boxes in #76513b, #987052 and #c3a575 at different tilts over the torso, with ragged edges. Hide trousers and give fur boots with leg wraps. Keep the hooked staff, but make the hook a clear crook: 3 short segments curving back down.
